answer: The Atlas tariff burns quadratically as a root multiplies. Each minted name is charged one hundred copper times the square of how many identities that funding source already produced: the second clone pays 400, the tenth 10,000, the fiftieth 250,000. A hundred-clone farm therefore incinerates 33,835,000 copper before its first payout, while Umber, a solo trader minting one honest name, keeps her cost at the flat hundred.
